Current Alzheimer's disease treatments fall into several complementary categories. Medications approved by the U.S. FDA include acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, galantamine, rivastigmine) for early to mid-stage disease and memantine for moderate to severe stages, with rivastigmine also available as a patch [d1,d5,d7]. Newer anti‑amyloid monoclonal antibodies (lecanemab and donanemab) are approved for early Alzheimer's and can slow decline in thinking and functioning [d4,d6,d8]. Non‑drug supports such as structured routines, safe environments, and caregiver strategies help manage daily life and behavioral symptoms [d2,d3]. Some approaches like herbal remedies and supplements lack strong evidence and are not supported as effective treatments [d2]. Ongoing research targets amyloid and other disease mechanisms, with investigational drugs like buntanetap under study [d9].
